gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named tester's measured heat-shutdown or dropout figure for any CarPlay screen. The best one found is TechTesting's: its Pioneer SPH-DA160DAB in-dash unit shut down after 45 minutes of continuous use at 28°C and dropped CarPlay four times in one hour-long motorway drive, while its reverse-camera input worked but looked washed out.
standout_why: I read CarTechTalk (#2, 2026-10-19), RottenWiFi (#4), CarAssists (#7), CarCody (#8) and GearNudge (#10). None of them gives a measured figure. Their brightness numbers (550 cd/m², 650 nits, 500 nits) are maker or listing claims, and GearNudge says it ran no lab tests. The TechTesting figures are new against these pages, but they are weak. They cover a UK in-dash Pioneer and an ATOTO, not the portable screens ChatGPT showed (ESSGOO, Easyonlife). The page names no tester for each test, gives no test dates and discloses paid placement. The pages most likely to hold real lab numbers are Car and Driver (#1) and Autoweek (#3), both titled 'Tested', and I could not open either. If they contain measurements, the rivals may already have this angle covered. I also could not read DashGear Lab (#5, #6) or ScoutVetted (#11) because of certificate errors.
decides: It does not decide the pick. None of the portable candidates (ESSGOO 10.26-inch, Easyonlife 10.26-inch, Carpuride W903, Intellidash Pro X10, IIWEY iK7, Krunia 9.26-inch) has a named, openable measurement of brightness, connect time or reverse-camera switch time. At most, TechTesting's results back a caution about heat and dropouts on dash-mounted units, so the page should not claim a measured advantage for any candidate.
candidates: Easyonlife 10.26-inch wireless CarPlay screen with dash cam

findings.label: Thermal shutdown in continuous use
findings.value: Shut down after 45 min at 28°C ambient
findings.note: TechTesting's three-week daily-commute test. The author profile is Jason Saarinen, the tests are written as 'we', and no test date is given. The page says companies pay for listings. This is an in-dash UK unit, not a portable screen.

findings.label: Wireless CarPlay dropouts
findings.value: 4 disconnects in one hour-long motorway drive (Android Auto: 2 on the same route)
findings.note: Counted by TechTesting during the commute test. The page says the reverse-camera input 'functioned properly' but the image looked washed out. That is a qualitative remark, not a measurement.

findings.label: Overheating and dropouts
findings.value: Overheated and dimmed after 90 min of navigation at 24°C; wireless CarPlay dropped twice in 30 min
findings.note: TechTesting one-month test of an in-dash unit. The page does not mention a backup camera for it. The page's prices are mismatched between scorecards (£489.90 / £249.00), so I give no price.

findings.label: Connection stability and setup time
findings.value: Held a wireless connection for over 4 h on the motorway (iPhone 15 Pro); setup took 10 min
findings.note: Portable unit with backup-camera support that switches to the rear view with guidelines in reverse. The page gives no timing method. This is a UK listing at £79.00 on the scorecard, not a US price.

unsourced: Car and Driver's and Autoweek's 'Best Portable CarPlay Screens, Tested' figures (results #1 and #3). WebFetch refuses caranddriver.com and autoweek.com, the search tool rejects these Hearst domains, and Bash curl was not approved. I could not see whether they publish lux, nits or timing figures.

Intellidash Pro X10 at '9,495 lux' against budget screens at '6,287 lux', and Carpuride W103 at a '19-second average startup'. Both appear on cartechstudio.com with no measurer, method or date, and an exact-phrase search for the lux figure found no original source.

Any independent review or measurement of the ESSGOO 10.26-inch (1026SCP / TS0001) or the Easyonlife 10.26-inch, the two products ChatGPT showed. Searches returned only retailer listings and short customer comments.

Measured reverse-camera switch time (seconds from shifting into reverse to the image) for any candidate. Carpuride W903 searches returned only user anecdotes, and MotorVerso's W903 review (Paul Hadley, 2025-04-25) has no timings and used only the front dash cam.

Brightness measured in nits with a meter for any portable candidate. Every nits figure I found (Krunia 550, CarpodGo 700/1,000, ATOTO P9 500) is a maker or listing spec. DubCorner's Krunia review (2026-03-26) gives only 'a second or two' as an unmeasured estimate of boot delay.

DashGear Lab (results #5, #6) and ScoutVetted (#11) failed on self-signed certificate errors, GearDiary's CarpodGo review returned 403, and the pulse.bot copy of the Road & Track test closed the connection. I could not check any of them for measurements.
